sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current official documentation, unpinned

sources.applicability: Mature sync alternative and attachment cost control.

sources.released_version_or_commit: Current official documentation as retrieved 2026-10-12; unpinned

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL requires same-host access, has one writer, and treats the WAL as database state. NORMAL can lose committed transactions after power failure. sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned official documentation reopened 2026-10-12; current SQLite release separately identified as 3.54.0 (S04).
sources.locator: Overview; How WAL Works; Concurrency; Performance Considerations; The WAL File; The WAL-Reset Bug (§11).
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official SQLite WAL documentation and inspected the captured sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL allows readers and a writer concurrently but only one writer per file; all database processes must be on the same host because the wal-index uses shared memory; checkpointing is automatic by default around 1000 pages but long readers can prevent completion; the WAL file is persistent database state and must accompany the main file; WAL durability depends on synchronous settings. The WAL-reset corruption race applied through SQLite 3.51.2 and is fixed in 3.51.3 and later.
sources.applicability: Supports SQLite as a local transactional store, while ruling out a shared network-file WAL and raw main-file copying. It also yields a minimum version-history check for any WAL candidate.

sources.title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
sources.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned official documentation; applicable mechanics reopened with SQLite 3.54.0 documentation set.
sources.locator: Introduction; Hardware Assumptions; Testing Atomic Commit Behavior (§8).
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official atomic-commit article.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Atomicity means all changes in one database transaction happen or none do, including interrupted commits under stated filesystem/OS assumptions. The detailed single-file rollback-journal walkthrough is explicitly for rollback mode; WAL uses a different mechanism. Crash tests simulate filesystem/power-loss damage and verify all-or-nothing transaction recovery and integrity.
sources.applicability: Supports one-laptop save atomicity as a primitive. It does not merge laptop histories or establish photo-file/database cross-resource atomicity.

sources.title: SQLite Online Backup API
sources.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned official documentation reopened 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Using the SQLite Online Backup API (§1); Other Backup Techniques (§1.1); Online Backup of a Running Database (§3).
sources.observed_operation: Opened the backup documentation and read the snapshot, copy, and error-handling conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A completed online backup is a bitwise-identical snapshot from the start of the operation. Incremental backup allows writers between reads; concurrent source writes may cause restart, and continuous restarts can prevent completion. Direct external copy can block writers or leave a corrupted destination after power/OS failure.
sources.applicability: A database-aware backup can support coherent manual transfer of a snapshot. It is not by itself a change merge or a replacement for an import receipt.

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Replication aims to copy active documents and propagate source deletions when documents are deleted through tombstone revisions. Content-dependent replication filters may not receive deleted content; a special _deleted:true field preserves content for filter evaluation but also retains record data and attachments. PouchDB implements the CouchDB replication algorithm for offline client use.
sources.applicability: Supports an offline replication alternative while informing delete, tombstone-retention, and photo-privacy design.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.released_version_or_commit: Unversioned official documentation reopened 2026-10-12; current SQLite release separately identified as 3.54.0 (S04).
sources.locator: Overview; How WAL Works; Concurrency; Performance Considerations; The WAL File; The WAL-Reset Bug (§11).
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official SQLite WAL documentation and inspected the captured sections.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL allows readers and a writer concurrently but only one writer per file; all database processes must be on the same host because the wal-index uses shared memory; checkpointing is automatic by default around 1000 pages but long readers can prevent completion; the WAL file is persistent database state and must accompany the main file; WAL durability depends on synchronous settings. The WAL-reset corruption race applied through SQLite 3.51.2 and is fixed in 3.51.3 and later.
sources.applicability: Supports SQLite as a local transactional store, while ruling out a shared network-file WAL and raw main-file copying. It also yields a minimum version-history check for any WAL candidate.
sources.critic_observed_operation: Opened WAL page; examined concurrency, checkpoint, WAL-file state, same-host constraint and WAL-reset/version conditions.

sources.observed_operation: Opened the official CouchDB conflict documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Revision branches retain concurrent leaves; a deterministic winner is shown by ordinary GET; clients must request conflicts/open revisions to inspect all tips. Conflict resolution explicitly updates one branch and deletes other leaf revisions. Compaction discards non-leaf bodies but retains revision identifiers, subject to revision pruning.
sources.applicability: Candidate replication model and warning that winner display, complete human history, and field-level merges require application code.
sources.critic_observed_operation: Opened CouchDB conflict docs; inspected ordinary GET, deterministic winner, conflict request and revision-tree/compaction context.

reviser_independent_recheck.condition: Basic GET returns only the deterministic winner without indicating hidden conflicts; conflict options expose other revision IDs and callers fetch leaves. Compaction drops non-leaf bodies and revision pruning exists.
reviser_independent_recheck.applicability: SCW-03: ordinary reads can conceal alternatives; a review UI must explicitly retrieve branches. Candidate library behavior is not product policy.

sources.title: CouchDB Replication Introduction

sources.observed_operation: Opened official replication documentation and read deletion/filter conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Replication aims to copy active documents and propagate source deletions when documents are deleted through tombstone revisions. Content-dependent replication filters may not receive deleted content; a special _deleted:true field preserves content for filter evaluation but also retains record data and attachments. PouchDB implements the CouchDB replication algorithm for offline client use.
sources.applicability: Supports an offline replication alternative while informing delete, tombstone-retention, and photo-privacy design.
sources.critic_observed_operation: Opened CouchDB replication intro; inspected deletion revision, content-dependent filter condition, and deleted-content workaround.

reviser_independent_recheck.observed_operation: Reopened CouchDB 3.5 stable Replication Introduction §§2.1.3–2.1.5; inspected deletion-revision propagation and filter conditions.
reviser_independent_recheck.condition: Deletion is represented as a new revision and propagated to target. Only content-dependent filters may lack old document content for a deleted revision; the _deleted:true workaround retains data and attachments.
reviser_independent_recheck.applicability: SCW-02: condition must remain scoped to content-dependent filters; ordinary unfiltered tombstone propagation is separately documented.

sources.observed_operation: Opened official Automerge merge-rule reference.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Different map keys combine; deleting a key while another peer makes no change removes it; deleting a key while another peer sets it yields the set value; concurrent sets choose a deterministic value. Concurrent list insertions/deletions use stable element IDs.
sources.applicability: Shows why observation deletion must be modeled as an explicit conflict/tombstone and not a bare map-key deletion.
sources.critic_observed_operation: Opened Automerge merge rules; confirmed rules are scoped to nested maps/lists and concurrent map delete/set behavior.

reviser_independent_recheck.applicability: SCW-05: C is supported as motivation for app-level tombstones; C* is neither specified nor contradicted for an observation-level tombstone.

sources.title: SQLite transaction control
sources.version: Current SQLite documentation; no release pin

sources.access_utc: 2026-10-12T00:39:51Z (clock immediately before the open batch; page fetch followed in the same call)
sources.observed_operation: Opened official transaction documentation; read writer concurrency, deferred upgrade, immediate-lock, and busy conditions.
sources.condition: Default transactions are DEFERRED; multiple readers are allowed but only one write transaction at a time. BEGIN IMMEDIATE begins a write transaction immediately and can return SQLITE_BUSY when another writer is active.
sources.applicability: Single-host booking authority; acquire the write reservation before availability check and handle busy/conflict outcomes.

records.title: CouchDB replication introduction
records.version_or_commit: Current stable documentation for CouchDB 3.5; release notes identify 3.5.3
records.locator: Transient/persistent replication; procedure; master-master; migrating data to clients
records.observed_operation: Read replication directions, checkpoints and filter conditions.
records.conditions_defaults_exceptions: Each replication is directional; bidirectional sync needs two replications; deletes replicate as new revisions; content-based filters see deleted docs without their original body; a workaround retaining all data is noted.
records.applicability: Supports comparison with application-server queues and identifies deletion/filter safety limits.

records.title: CouchDB conflict model
records.version_or_commit: Current stable documentation for CouchDB 3.5; release notes identify 3.5.3
records.locator: Sections conflict avoidance, revision trees, working with conflicting documents and views
records.observed_operation: Read normal write rejection, winner visibility, conflict retrieval and app-specific merge behavior.
records.conditions_defaults_exceptions: Same-node stale revision can return 409; replicas may retain branches; ordinary GET/view expose the deterministic winner; application must inspect and resolve branches; compaction drops non-leaf bodies.
records.applicability: Supports caution that replication and deterministic winner selection are not a domain resolution.

records.title: CouchDB changes-feed API
records.version_or_commit: Current stable documentation for CouchDB 3.5; release notes identify 3.5.3
records.locator: Query parameters include_docs, attachments, style; _changes defaults
records.observed_operation: Read feed modes and defaults affecting sync, conflict visibility and attachments.
records.conditions_defaults_exceptions: include_docs=false and attachments=false by default; include_docs with conflicts still returns only the winner; main_only is the default style; base64 inline attachments have overhead and only recent changes per doc are guaranteed.
records.applicability: Supports summary/sync design and the recommendation not to inline large photo bytes in the change feed.

records.title: CouchDB database security API
records.version_or_commit: Current stable documentation for CouchDB 3.5; release notes identify 3.5.3
records.locator: GET/PUT database security object; members and admins
records.observed_operation: Read database member/admin permissions and default behavior.
records.conditions_defaults_exceptions: Members read all document types in the database and write ordinary documents; an empty member/role set can leave ordinary docs readable/writable; new CouchDB 3.x databases default admin-only.
records.applicability: Shows database membership is not record-level privacy; keep contact data out of shared records or mediate by narrower API.

records.title: CouchDB authentication API
records.version_or_commit: Current stable documentation for CouchDB 3.5; release notes identify 3.5.3
records.locator: Proxy Authentication and JWT Authentication sections
records.observed_operation: Read external identity integration options and required configuration.
records.conditions_defaults_exceptions: Proxy auth must be enabled in the active handler list and strongly recommends a shared secret; JWT auth requires trusted signing keys and required claims. Neither identifies the center's current identity provider.
records.applicability: Supports possible integration with an existing organizational IdP while keeping identity choice unresolved.

records.title: CouchDB attachment API

records.locator: PUT and DELETE attachment endpoints; revision conditions; range requests
records.observed_operation: Read attachment upload/download/delete requirements and response conditions.
records.conditions_defaults_exceptions: Updating/deleting an attachment updates the parent revision; an existing document requires current revision information; deletion requires rev or If-Match; Range requests are documented for reads.
records.applicability: Supports conflict-aware, optional attachment workflow; does not prove resumable upload semantics.

sources.locator: Fragment Selector §4.2.2; Text Position Selector §4.2.10 (lines 980–1010); Target/Specific Resource and State sections

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Text positions are zero-based start-inclusive/end-exclusive. The model says they are brittle after edits and recommends a State to identify the correct representation; selectors describe target segments but do not create time synchronization.

sources.title: HTML Standard: media elements
sources.version_or_commit: WHATWG Living Standard; snapshot accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: §4.8.11.6 lines 1798–1859 (duration/currentTime/timeline); §4.8.11.9 lines 2401–2479 (seekable, fastSeek, seeking algorithm)
sources.observed_operation: Direct open and find in the WHATWG standard
sources.governing_condition_or_default_or_except: duration is seconds, NaN when unavailable and Infinity for unbounded streams. currentTime is seconds on the resource's media timeline; setting it seeks. fastSeek trades precision for speed. Seeking clamps to source bounds and, when outside seekable ranges, chooses a nearest seekable point; seeking is asynchronous.
sources.applicability: A concrete example of why player adapters must report readiness/seek completion and actual position, and why time precision must not be inferred from decimal formatting. Local recordings normally have finite durations, but player/media metadata still governs actual seek results.

sources.title: SQLite Transactions

sources.title: SQLite UPSERT
sources.release_or_commit: SQLite UPSERT added in 3.24.0; generalized in 3.35.0; docs updated 2024-04-11
sources.locator: Conflict target and DO UPDATE semantics; §4 History.
sources.observed_operation: Opened documentation and inspected conflict-update semantics and version history.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: UPSERT chooses behavior on a uniqueness/primary-key conflict; DO UPDATE changes the conflicting row. Constraint violations in the DO UPDATE path abort the INSERT statement.
sources.applicability: Can support a unique import-batch/row ledger if SQLite is used; uniqueness keys must reflect supplier, file/profile and row identity, not a bare supplier product code.
sources.evidence_limitations: A database UPSERT alone does not define inventory snapshot-vs-delta semantics or make application logic idempotent.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 COPY
sources.locator: COPY FROM options ON_ERROR, REJECT_LIMIT, LOG_VERBOSITY, ENCODING; CSV NULL/header handling.
sources.observed_operation: Opened PostgreSQL 18 reference and inspected default error action and reject reporting options.

sources.applicability: Conditional server-database bulk-staging alternative. If used, land raw data in a private staging table and preserve rejected-row detail; don't use ignore as a substitute for reviewable row outcomes.
sources.evidence_limitations: No PostgreSQL backend was supplied; conversion-error handling does not define application identity, business validation, or all structural CSV errors.

sources.title: SQLite transaction semantics

sources.title: Koha Manual — Circulation
sources.version_or_commit: Manual edition 20261011
sources.locator: Check out lines 22–100; automatic check-in lines 495–499; Claim returned lines 614–631; bundle add/circulation/checkin/missing sections lines 697–785
sources.observed_operation: Checkout scans item barcode; optional keyword fallback. Automatic checkin requires item-type configuration and automatic_checkin.pl cron. Bundle return scans expected child barcodes; missing children are marked lost and tied to a claim. Claim-return entry accepts note and fee decision.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Item barcode fallback is a preference; automatic checkin is optional. Bundle verification can be skipped. Missing-as-lost is configurable. Claim returned is a patron report about a loan, not a general correction ledger.
sources.applicability: Strong kit/circulation fit; configure no automatic return and test atomic damage hold and durable correction history.

sources.title: Snipe-IT Asset model
sources.version_or_commit: v8.8.0 tag, release commit 2c466fa
sources.locator: availableForCheckout lines around 3124–3173; checkOut around 3200–3294
sources.observed_operation: Model gates availability on not assigned, not deleted, status deployable and not archived; checkout stores expected check-in and optional note.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A checked-out asset may retain due date/note, but source does not guarantee general immutable correction history or damaged-return atomicity.
sources.applicability: Source-level confirmation of identity/status predicate; test check-in/status transitions in product.

critic_verification.critic_status: independently reopened
critic_verification.critic_observation: Confirmed checkout availability requires unassigned/undeleted and deployable/non-archived status. Separately, check-in eligibility requires an assigned asset and, apart from the deleted-asset exception, a deployable/non-archived status. The caller/order was not independently traced; do not infer a product defect from the predicate alone.

reviser_verification.version_or_commit: Snipe-IT v8.8.0 tag; carried release commit 2c466fa

reviser_verification.access_utc: 2026-10-12T01:25:03Z–2026-10-12T01:25:22Z; exact per-request fetch timestamp was not exposed

reviser_verification.applicability: Keep the check-in/maintenance sequence unresolved and test the exact release-pinned UI/API path plus a concurrent checkout; do not infer a defect from the predicate alone.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.version_or_commit: SQLite official online docs, accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: WAL limitations, lines/paragraphs on network filesystems and one writer
sources.observed_operation: WAL shared-memory index requires processes on same host; WAL does not work over a network filesystem; one writer at a time.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL-specific constraints; SQLite has other modes, but a shared file DB is still not the preferred two-host authority.
sources.applicability: Reject a naive shared SQLite file as the concurrent laptop deployment design.

critic_verification.critic_status: independently reopened
critic_verification.critic_observation: Confirmed WAL index access relies on a shared mapped file in the database directory and the documented no-shared-memory mode requires a single process; the draft scopes this as a constraint on shared/network use.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 17 Explicit Locking
sources.version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 17 documentation
sources.locator: §13.3 row-level lock modes, FOR UPDATE
sources.observed_operation: FOR UPDATE locks selected rows against conflicting writes/locks until transaction ends.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Application must use one transaction with revalidation/unique constraints and handle deadlocks; database row locks alone do not define product workflow.
sources.applicability: Basis for a local authoritative service/custom architecture candidate.

critic_verification.critic_status: independently reopened
critic_verification.critic_observation: Confirmed FOR UPDATE blocks conflicting writes and locks on the same row until transaction end.

sources.title: Koha Manual — damaged and not-for-loan statuses
sources.version_or_commit: Manual edition 20261011
sources.locator: Damaged status lines 3034–3078; not-for-loan status lines 3142–3200; AllowNotForLoanOverride preference lines 683–696 in circulationpreferences.html
sources.observed_operation: Damaged status makes search results unavailable but does not stop checkout/check-in. Not-for-loan status blocks checkout unless staff override is permitted; override default is Allow. Positive values prevent checkout and holds; configured check-in mapping only updates existing not-for-loan state.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: To make a hard hold, configure a not-for-loan status and disallow overrides; damaged flag by itself is not a hold. The status mapping is not a damage-to-hold workflow, so a status transition may need explicit staff action and must be race-tested.
sources.applicability: Critical fit limitation for the damaged-return requirement; do not accept Koha without a tested one-step hold workflow.

critic_verification.critic_status: independently reopened
critic_verification.critic_observation: Confirmed damaged flag does not block checkout/check-in, the not-for-loan override default is Allow, and check-in mapping applies to a matching existing not-for-loan value.
